content: Morley is a fictional cigarette brand, seemingly inspired by the name Marlboro, and has been featured in numerous television shows and films. Below are detailed instances of its appearances: In the movie 200 Cigarettes, Lucy, played by Courtney Love, gives Kevin, portrayed by Paul Rudd, a block of Morley cigarettes. The film's title refers to the total number of cigarettes in a carton (20 cigarettes per pack, 10 packs per carton). In the online animated series Broken Saints, the character Raimi purchases a pack of Morley cigarettes. Interestingly, William B. Davis, known for his role in The X-Files, is part of the voice cast. However, the series' creator, Brooke Burgess, clarified that the inclusion of Morley cigarettes predated Davis's involvement, though he appreciated the reference. In Buffy the Vampire Slayer, the character Spike, played by James Marsters, is seen smoking Morley cigarettes. Marsters was mistakenly quoted as saying that both he and William B. Davis's characters (from The X-Files) smoked Morleys, making them the only two TV characters to do so. In the Cold Case episode The Plan, a character named Jerry smokes Morley cigarettes. During an interrogation scene, Detective Nick Vera removes a cigarette from Jerry's hand after it burns down to his fingers. In the Criminal Minds episode North Mammon, a pile of Morley cigarette butts leads the FBI team to suspect a soccer coach of stalking one of his players. DNA analysis of the cigarette butts implicates him. However, upon closer inspection of the episode, the cigarette pack shown is actually a Marlboro pack, not a Morley. In the ER episode Beyond Repair, Morley cigarettes make an appearance. In the film Freddy Got Fingered, the character Gord, played by Tom Green, is seen smoking a pack of Morleys in one scene. In the movie Gun Shy, a box of Morley cigarettes is visible on the conference table during a meeting between police officers. In the 1970 TV movie House on Greenapple Road, a character steals a pack of Morley cigarettes from a desk at the police station. In the series Jake 2.0, a terrorist disguises powerful explosives as a pack of Morley cigarettes and demonstrates their destructive power by detonating a piece of swamp in the Philippines. In the Killer Instinct episode Game Over, Lt. Matt Cavanaugh, played by Chi McBride, has Morley cigarettes visible on his desk. In an episode of Malcolm in the Middle, a pack of Morley cigarettes is one of the items hidden by Malcolm's mother. In the Millennium episode The Time Is Now, Peter Watts finds a Morley cigarette stub in the Millennium Group's basement. This is a nod to the Cigarette Smoking Man from The X-Files, as both series were created by Chris Carter. In the original Mission Impossible television series, Morley cigarettes appear, with several characters seen holding them. In the Nash Bridges episode Power Play, a pack of Morleys is visible on a desk in a criminal's house. In Prison Break season 2, episode 11, T-Bag picks up a pack of Morleys from a bag in Roy's apartment. In an episode of The Outer Limits, a man boarding a bus is seen holding a pack of Morley cigarettes. In the film Prozac Nation, Christina Ricci's character smokes Morley cigarettes. Her character, a young writer, occasionally uses the empty cigarette packs as scrap paper. In the Space: Above and Beyond episode Ray Butts, the titular character is seen with a pack of Morleys at the beginning of the episode. In the Special Unit 2 episode The Grain, a housewife under the influence of the Sandman robs a convenience store, demanding cash and a pack of Morley cigarettes. In the movie Spy Game, Morley cigarettes make an appearance. In That '70s Show episode Eric Gets Suspended, Red Forman forces Eric to smoke an entire pack of Morleys after catching him with a cigarette at school. In the film Thirteen, Morley cigarettes are featured. In the Twilight Zone episode Nightmare at 20,000 Feet (September 1963), William Shatner's character pulls out a pack of Morley cigarettes and almost lights one before his wife points out the illuminated NO SMOKING sign on the plane. This is the earliest known reference to Morley cigarettes. In The X-Files, the Cigarette Smoking Man, played by William B. Davis, is frequently seen smoking Morley cigarettes. This is perhaps the most iconic use of the fictional brand. In one episode, Mulder and Scully even visit Morley's headquarters after an employee is murdered. These appearances highlight the recurring use of Morley cigarettes as a fictional prop in various media, often as a subtle nod or Easter egg for viewers.
